newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA - TALLINN BOURSE TO TIGHTEN FREE MARKET RULES.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA - TALLINN BOURSE TO TIGHTEN FREE MARKET RULES.

text.p: TALLINN, March 27 (Reuter) The Tallinn stock exchange board said on Thursday that it will introduce information requirements for companies listed on the free market.

"The board decided that the same information requirments for listed companies will be applied to companies on the free market," Helo Meigas, the managing director of the Tallinn stock exchange, told Reuters.
"We decided on the move because of the inadequacy of existing legistation and the need to protect investors," she said.
Meigas said that the new provisions will also mean stricter information requirements for companies seeking to be traded on the free market.
"The only difference between companies on the main list and those on the free market will be that those on the free market will not pay a listing fee," she said.
"The decision will also mean that companies on the free market and those coming to the free market will be required to seek entry on main list after one year of trading on the free market," she said.
"The companies listed on the free market now will not have any problems with the new requirements and it should encourage some companies to be more active on the market," one trader said.
The rules are expected to come into force in mid-May.
